name: Ampicillin + sulbactam
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Ampicillin and sulbactam are both about 75% to 85% excreted unchanged in urine, and kidney impairment slows both equally, so their ratio stays constant. The US label gives 1.5 to 3 g at longer intervals as creatinine clearance (CrCl) falls: every 6 to 8 hours at 30 or more, every 12 hours at 15–29 and every 24 hours at 5–14 mL/min/1.73 m2. The label gives no dialysis dose.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses CrCl in mL/min/1.73 m2 (Cockcroft–Gault formula quoted); bands at 30 and 15.

bands.recommendation: 1.5 to 3 g every 6 hours (usual); the label's CrCl 30 or more row allows every 6 to 8 hours (label Table 3).
CrCl 30 or more: 1.5 to 3 g every 6 to 8 hours (label Table 3).
CrCl 15–29: 1.5 to 3 g every 12 hours (label Table 3).
CrCl 5–14: 1.5 to 3 g every 24 hours (label Table 3). Below 5: not stated; specialist input.

hd: No hemodialysis dosing in label. Ampicillin is removed by hemodialysis, and sulbactam probably is (label overdose section). Specialist input.
pd: No peritoneal dialysis dosing in label. Specialist input.
crrt: Not in label. Li 2020 (Table 3), sulbactam component: CVVH ultrafiltration 30 mL/kg/h, CVVHD dialysate 1 L/h, or CVVHDF combined 1 L/h, 1 g every 8 hours; higher doses may be needed for less susceptible organisms, and Li suggests drug level monitoring.
dialyzable: Ampicillin: yes, removed by hemodialysis. Sulbactam: probably, from its size, protein binding and kinetics (label). Protein binding: ampicillin 28%, sulbactam 38%.
monitoring: CrCl for dose; seizures with high CSF beta-lactam levels (label overdose section); liver tests (history of cholestatic jaundice is a contraindication); rash; diarrhea (CDAD).

pediatric.approved_ages: 1 year and older (skin and skin structure infections, IV) (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: 300 mg/kg/day IV (200 mg ampicillin plus 100 mg sulbactam per kg), divided every 6 hours; 40 kg or more: adult dose (label).
pediatric.max_dose: Sulbactam 4 g/day; IV course usually not over 14 days (label).

renal.recommendation: No pediatric kidney dosing in label. Specialist input.

High-dose sulbactam regimens for Acinetobacter are not in the label and are not drafted.
